# NOTES ON THE TWO BOOKS (use these instead of the source text)

## BOOK 1 of 2: THE RUNAWAYS (Nat Gould, Gutenberg #39631)

**Front matter:** Appreciation by E. Laton Blacklands (Gould b. Manchester 1857, d. 1919; journalist in England/Australia; hobbies racing, driving, gardening; Times obituary quoted). Publisher: G. Heath Robinson & J. Birch, Ltd.

**Contents:** I As the Snow Falls (11); II The Runaways (23); III Random (35); IV Irene's Painting (45); V Honeysuckle's Foal (57); VI A Wily Young Man (70); VII Selling His Heritage (83); VIII Warren's Return (96); IX How Ulick Bought the Saint (108); X "The Curiosity" (120); XI For a Woman's Sake (133); XII Two Schemers (146); XIII The Squire and the Saint (158); XIV A Discovery Imminent (170); XV The Result of the Discovery (182); XVI A Race to be Remembered (194); XVII The Squire Overhears (206); XVIII "Tally-Ho!" (219); XIX A Fatal Leap (230); XX Perfect Harmony (242).

**Characters:**
- Redmond Maynard, "the Squire," of Hazelwell; widower-type proud man; guardian of Irene.
- Ulick Maynard, his son; left home two years earlier after bitter quarrel (father accused him of wronging Janet Todd; Ulick: "Believing, as you must... I will no longer inflict my presence upon you, sir. Good-night.").
- Bersak, Squire's wolf-hound (saved Ulick from bull).
- Irene Courtly (née Carstone), daughter of Colonel Carstone; ward of Squire from age 16; married Warren Courtly ~18 months before; painter; rides Rupert (dark brown) and Random (bay hunter, Ulick's favourite; she painted him).
- Warren Courtly, of Anselm Manor (monastery origin, Henry VIII deed); gambler; sold Holme Farm for £10,000; secretly kept Janet at Feltham.
- Eli Todd, stud manager, ex-Hussars with Colonel Carstone; daughter Janet Todd (vain, pretty).
- Mrs. Marley (Hazelwell housekeeper); Mary Marley (Irene's maid, later marries Bob Heather); Bob Heather (groom, drives "the tub").
- Martha Dixon, Anselm housekeeper.
- Dr. Harding (doctor); James Bard (vet, Helton); Sam Lane (huntsman); Joe (Eli's helper); Josh (publican at Hazelwell?/ale).
- Felix Hoffman, racecourse tout/swindler, Feltham, Main St no.25; mother Mrs. Hoffman (widow-in-fact; husband Milas, jeweller, fled).
- Fred May, trainer (Stanton House, Newmarket); Ben Sprig, jockey (olive green colours); Conrad Rush (owner Kit Cat); Lucas Savell not here.
- Janet's "Mrs. Warren" name at Feltham; Moggs-type characters absent here.

**Horses:** Honeysuckle (old mare, Oaks & St Leger winner; colt foal born 12:15 after midnight New Year's Day, Eli, Ulick present); The Saint (grey, "the curiosity," by Father Confessor out of Hilda; owned by Ulick as "Mr. Lanark," bought 200 guineas via May); Random; Rupert; Vulture (American, Derby winner); Pinkerton; Kit Cat; Sandstone (Derby winner, Warren's bet); Coralie; Avenger; Decoy Duck; Mermaid; Milander.

**Events in order:**
1. Snowy night, two years after Ulick left; Squire at window, Bersak; Irene arrives on foot, stays at Hazelwell (Warren in London).
2. Backstory: Ulick accused, left; Janet vanished same night; Eli's scene with Squire ("hussey" word, Eli protests).
3. Squire sits up all night on anniversary; Irene paints Random; Warren's letter with scented paper, "et cetera."
4. Irene reads Felix Hoffman begging letter, sends £5; Holme Farm sale announced.
5. New Year's Eve: Honeysuckle foals; Ulick secretly visits Eli, leaves for London; gives address; owns the Saint.
6. Felix's background; meets Warren at Hurst Park (Milander tip); Warren places Janet at Mrs Hoffman's, Feltham, as "Mrs Warren," £3/week.
7. Warren sells Holme Farm (£10,000) for debts; Janet demands money.
8. Warren tells Irene of gambling; Irene shows Felix letter; Warren furious.
9. Ulick sees Saint win Pastures Handicap at Kempton (beats Pinkerton, Kit Cat third); sees Janet at Feltham, meets her; sees Warren there, realises truth.
10. Squire and Eli scheme; reconciliation at Stanton House, Newmarket; Ulick refuses to return yet.
11. Dinner at Walton Hotel; Ulick and Irene on balcony.
12. Felix blackmails Warren £50; Felix writes to Irene (£100 demand); Irene visits Feltham, meets Janet (confession).
13. Irene confronts Warren at Walton; Derby day (Sandstone wins); Coronation Cup (Saint beats Vulture by short head).
14. Felix insults Warren in paddock; Squire overhears "two wives"; Warren confesses to Irene; rides off, returns.
15. Warren's jump: rides grey Irish horse at Glen church wall (Hunt, Tone river, fox) to dare Ulick; grey falls onto Harewood's vault; Warren's neck broken. Irene and Squire find him. Burial at Anselm.
16. Janet returns to Eli. Ulick and Irene marry after a year; Janet becomes Irene's maid; child born; Felix flees the country.

**Key quotations:** "Bersak, where's Ulick?"; "Believing, as you must..."; "Irene, this is your home."

---

## BOOK 2 of 2: TINMAN (Tom Gallon, Gutenberg #48989)

**Front matter:** Title page; Boston: Small, Maynard & Co., 1907.

**Structure:** Part I (Ch I–VI), Part II (Ch I–XIII).

**Narrator:** Charles Avaline, first-person; written in prison/garret; ward of Jervis Fanshawe. Later called "Tinman," "No. 145."

**Characters:**
- Charles Avaline (narrator; b. ~20; artist; Bloomsbury; later convict No. 145, "Tinman").
- Jervis Fanshawe, guardian; manager of Patton & Co.; cruel, embezzler; hates Barbara; kills Murray Olivant in Part II (confesses; sails on the *Eaglet*, lost in wreck; Murray's body buried in pauper's grave).
- Gavin Hockley, big young man, swaggering, moustache; gambler; killed by Charles with a sword in Lincoln's Inn Fields (Charles's first murder). Hockley's lie: Barbara "a lady of many loves."
- Barbara Patton (daughter of old Patton, Hammerstone Market); marries Lucas Savell (cousin, good-humoured, weak); wedding day; note "Because I love you and trust you..."; signed "BARBARA"; calls Charlie "my poor Prince Charlie."
- Mr. Patton (old, white-haired, dies later).
- Mrs. Dixon? No — characters at Patton house: elderly sister, Dr. and wife, Lucas Savell.
- Murray Olivant, rich, cruel; half-brother of Arnold Millard; pursues Barbara Savell; sets up a "steamer trick" (*Eaglet*); killed in his Lincoln's Inn Fields rooms.
- Arnold Millard, painter, Charles's counterpart; loves Barbara Savell; threatens Olivant; leaves with her... ends up married to her.
- Barbara Savell (the daughter, "new Barbara," b. ~18 at story time).
- Dawkins, Olivant's friend; perpetual smile; kidnaps/sells Barbara's address for £500.
- Moggs, a shabby street girl (~15) at Fanshawe's lodging by the river; helps find Barbara.
- Mrs. Hoffman? No — that is Book 1.
- Barbara (first, the elder, "Barbara Avaline"/"Mrs. Avaline"): travelled back to save Charles; escapes Lucas Savell on ship; reunited with husband at end (Savell has stroke, dies, never speaks).
- Lucas Savell: husband of elder Barbara; drinks; stroke; dies.

**Events in order (Part I):**
1. Charles, aged 20, goes to London; Fanshawe's Bloomsbury dinner with Hockley.
2. Hammerstone Market (Fanshawe's patron Patton); meets Barbara in wood (painting), Hockley lounging, Fanshawe spying by pool.
3. Dinner at Patton's: Savell engagement to Barbara announced; Charles and Barbara on terrace; Hockley assaults her; Charles strikes Hockley down with a blow on temple, Hockley falls down steps.
4. Card game at Fanshawe's; Charles loses ~£30; Hockley taunts; Charles's I.O.U.s.
5. Wedding day; Barbara's note; burned.
6. Supper party at inn; Hockley's lie; Charles attacks him; Fanshawe takes Charles to Patton's.
7. Charles goes to Hockley's rooms in Lincoln's Inn Fields; kills him with old sword. Fanshawe admits he meant it (sent no cheque; Hockley had letters).
8. Arrest; trial; "Guilty"; death sentence; reprieved to penal servitude for life ("on account of my youth"). Barbara's dream visits; she comes to prison, promises silence.

**Part II:**
1. Twenty years in prison (No. 145; tinsmith); released; Fanshawe meets him at gates, renames him "Tinman."
2. London: Fanshawe's rooms by river; Charles goes to Hammerstone Market, sees the new Barbara (Barbara Savell) with Arnold Millard in wood; Savell is father.
3. Employed by Murray Olivant; sent to Hammerstone Market; ghost-like woman at terrace (elder Barbara, not dead—she was lost at sea by false report).
4. Olivant threatens; Charles threatens Olivant; Arnold Millard threatens Olivant.
5. Olivant's trick: Charles tied and gagged by Dawkins; forged note sends Barbara to London with Dawkins.
6. Charles escapes; meets elder Barbara (alive); Savell's drunken state; Fanshawe seen at garden.
7. Charles takes Olivant's place to Lincoln's Inn Fields; Dawkins's blackmail; Olivant threatens.
8. Moggs finds Barbara Savell at Fanshawe's? (Dawkins held); Barbara rescued to elder Barbara's lodging.
9. Olivant's "steamer trick"; Charles learns plan. Olivant's new rooms; Olivant found dead, knife in breast (killed by Fanshawe).
10. Charles at Olivant's rooms; Fanshawe confesses killing; sails on *Eaglet*; Charles's knife bought.
11. Charles returns to Hammerstone Market; elder Barbara returns to husband Lucas Savell; Savell suffers stroke and never speaks again.
12. Charles and Barbara reunite; Barbara remains with him. Charles reflects; Barbara Savell (new Barbara) marries Arnold Millard at Hammerstone Market; elder Barbara's words: "Let me take it now, and keep it to the end."

**Key quotations:** "Because I love you and trust you..."; "Hi! — I will reach you—God willing—before they kill you"; "Going always to be very brave and very gentle."

**Ending:** Charles and Barbara united; narrator poor and old; "a woman's hand steals over mine."
